1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Mahesh Chandra Shukla, learned counsel for the respondent complainant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant.
Subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was in love with the applicant and both of them had gone together.
She also stated that they have solemnised marriage.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that as per the radiological examination report, the age of the victim is around 17 years.
The victim has not supported the prosecution story in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

It is further submitted that admittedly the applicant Binu Rawat vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147154482/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and victim has solemnised marriage, hence, the applicant who is languishing in custody since 4.8.2023 having no criminal antecedents may be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent complainant as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

5. Considering the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in which the victim has not supported the prosecution story coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 4.8.2023 having no criminal antecedents without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Binu Rawat be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.292 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Para,
District Lucknow on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
